lead: The overnight batch keeps a reported AI-attributed eviction, competing sabotage claims and a lithography policy argument at their evidence level. An in-browser inference experiment and a plugin-design probe carry single-author measurement limits.

The late-morning batch pairs a vendor denial of sabotage claims with an unconfirmed encryption-break rumor, and keeps a bare-metal speed claim and a draft Pi provider at their evidence level. Two accounts of asynchronous agent work shift the human role to planning and review; Reddit's retention figures and Embo's robotics raise are company-reported.

sections.title: An automated assurance is not yet an adjudicated obligation
sections.intro: A reported eviction after AI-attributed rent emails raises disclosure and liability questions that remain factually and legally open.

sections.title: Sabotage allegations and a vendor denial both remain unverified
sections.intro: New social posts claim intentional interference while an Anthropic-affiliated response denies it; neither side's evidence was inspectable here.

sections.title: In-browser inference trades prompt speed for locality
sections.intro: An experimental WebAssembly engine approaches native generation speed on one machine while lagging badly on prompt processing.

sections.title: A model as API design probe
sections.intro: datasette-charts improved its plugin hook after a Claude-built prototype exposed friction points.

sections.title: Prediction tracking needs its own methodology check
sections.intro: A visible match example is not an accuracy rate, and the site's scoring was not reviewed.

sections.title: Export controls can strand the technology they guard
sections.intro: A lithography veteran argues the MATCH Act could hand serviced, reverse-engineerable scanners to rivals.

sections.title: A draft provider is not an endorsed integration
sections.intro: A pull request would wire Google AI plan sign-in into the Pi coding agent; claims of official approval appear only in unverified comments.

sections.title: A bare-metal LLM runtime credits its speed to removing Linux
sections.intro: A 24 KB assembly OS claims up to 54% faster token generation than llama.cpp, as a single-author demonstration of one small model.

sections.title: A vendor denial joins the sabotage dispute
sections.intro: Anthropic-affiliated Edwin Arbus answers sabotage allegations with an account of two days of non-visible safeguards in June; neither side's evidence is independently verifiable here.

sections.title: Encryption-break rumors remain unconfirmed
sections.intro: Nature reports rumors of AI breaking public-key cryptography while the published record shows only a subexponential factoring claim and calls for reproducibility.

sections.title: Agentic work moves the effort to planning and review
sections.intro: An experience report and a new multi-machine framework both assume agents work unattended, guarded by sandboxes, rules and pipelines rather than constant supervision.

sections.title: Reddit defends its logged-in moat and a robotics lab raises $110M
sections.intro: Reddit's COO argues seasoned logged-in users offset AI-search referral losses, while Embo launches with a large seed for video-pretrained robot world models; both are company accounts.
